item.title: CapitaLand Ascott Trust marks 20 years with earnings growth, active capital recycling and $8.9 bil assets
item.description: Twenty years after its listing, CapitaLand Ascott Trust (CLAS) has grown into Asia Pacific’s largest lodging trust, with total assets of $8.9 billion as at end-2025. For the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), CLAS reported an 11% year-on-year increase in income available for distribution to $256.7 million. item.title: PGIM Real Estate and Northstar Capital buy Tuas industrial site for $121.1 mil
item.description: PGIM Real Estate and Northstar Capital Logiprop, an entity of industrial and logistics development and management company Northstar Capital, have jointly acquired 51 Tuas View Link for $121.1 million. The private leasehold, non-JTC industrial site spans 456,810 sq ft and is zoned Business 2 (B2), allowing for both light and heavy industrial uses such as manufacturing, chemical processing and large-scale warehousing. item.title: Johor emerges as Malaysia’s second-largest residential market—JLL Malaysia
item.description: Johor has established itself as Malaysia’s second-largest residential market in 2025, following Selangor, based on both transaction volume and value. In 3Q2025, Johor recorded 10,500 transactions with a total value of RM5,487 million (S$1,769 million). The southern state sustained positive momentum, outperforming the national trend as well as other key markets. item.title: Apac real estate investment grew 13.7% in 2025, led by rebound in retail deals: Knight Frank
item.description: Real estate investment in the Asia Pacific (Apac) region grew in 2025, despite a lower volume recorded in the last quarter of the year. A January research report by Knight Frank shows that Apac real estate investment totalled US$56 billion ($70.9 billion) in 4Q2025, a 10% decrease from the previous quarter and a 7.4% decline y-o-y. item.title: GuocoLand books $85.4 mil earnings for 1HFY2026, up 14% y-o-y
item.description: GuocoLand recorded a 14% y-o-y increase in profit attributable to equity holders to $85.4 million for the first half ended Dec 31, 2025 (1HFY2026), despite a decline in revenue across the same period. Group revenue declined 22% y-o-y in 1HFY2026 to $791.9 million, due largely to the timing of progressive revenue recognition from residential projects under construction. item.title: Former JTC chief Tan Boon Khai to lead Therme Group’s $1 bil Marina South wellness resort project
item.description: Therme Group has appointed former JTC Corp chief Tan Boon Khai as CEO of Therme Group Singapore. In a Feb 2 press release, the developer says Tan will lead the development of Therme Singapore, its $1 billion wellness attraction at Marina South. Tan was CEO of JTC Corp between September 2020 and March 2025. Prior to that, he served as chief executive of the Singapore Land Authority and held senior roles at CapitaLand and The Ascott.
